items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee mentions Count Basie only in the context of discussing the style of the Count Basie Band and later references 'Basie' as a style guide ('Swing style. Basie.') given to him by older musicians, indicating knowledge of the band/style but no personal interaction.

ctx.x: Playing for dances. But you’re talking about the recording, but if we…

Herschel Evans might have had one song, but they did not have songs with Herschel Evans playing for fourteen minutes - song after song, after song, after song, after song. We can go get some bootlegs. It’s just you…. That’s not a successful formula, because, as much as people like to dance, it’s the melodies that attract them. Cause if it was Herschel, then they would have said, “Count Basie Band Featuring Herschel Evans.” Or, “The Herschel Evans Band Featuring Count Basie.” But it’s like the game inside the…

keep playing, and keep…. I remember… (laughs)…when Joey first joined the band. He was playing this tune and he wasn’t playing very well. And he said a…. He believed…. Well, he’s a gambler. He has a gambler’s mentality. “If I play one more chorus, I’m gonna find my way out of this shit.” So he says…. I’m sitting there and he’s dying. He’s dying.
